verses.text: Di vision of Isaiah, Amoz pikin, wey e see concerning Judah and Jerusalem for di days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, una heavens, and listen, earth, because di Lord don talk: “I don raise pikin dem and bring dem up, but dem don rebel against me.
Di ox know im owner, and di donkey know im master crib, but Israel no know, my people no understand.”

Ah, sinful nation, people wey dey carry heavy guilt, offspring of evildoers, pikin dem wey dey corrupt! Dem don leave di Lord, dem don despise di Holy One of Israel, dem don turn dem back go backward.
Why una go still dey beaten, una wey dey rebel more and more? Di whole head dey sick, and di whole heart dey faint.
From di sole of di foot even to di head, no soundness dey inside am, only wounds, bruises and open sores. Dem no close dem, no bandage dem, no soften dem with oil.
Your country don dey desolate, your cities don burn with fire. As for your land, strangers dey eat am before your eyes, and e dey desolate, like wetin strangers overthrow.
Di daughter of Zion dey left like shelter for vineyard, like lodge for cucumber field, like city wey dem don besiege.
Except di Lord of Armies leave us small remnant, we for don be like Sodom, we for don resemble Gomorrah.
Hear di word of di Lord, una rulers of Sodom! Listen to di law of our God, una people of Gomorrah!

“Wetin be di multitude of una sacrifices to me?” di Lord talk. “I don get enough of burnt offerings of rams, and di fat of well-fed animals. I no delight for di blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.
When una come to appear before me, who ask una to trample my courts?
No bring vain offerings again. Incense na abomination to me. New moon, Sabbath and di calling of assemblies; I no fit bear iniquity together with solemn assembly.
My soul hate una new moons and una appointed feasts. Dem don become burden to me. I don tire to carry dem.
When una spread out una hands, I go hide my eyes from una. Yes, when una make many prayers, I no go hear. Una hands full of blood.
Wash una, make una clean. Put away di evil of una doings from before my eyes. Stop to do evil.
Learn to do well. Seek justice. Rebuke di oppressor. Defend di fatherless. Plead for di widow.”
“Come now, make we reason together,” di Lord talk. “Though una sins be like scarlet, dem go be white as snow. Though dem red like crimson, dem go be like wool.
If una dey willing and obedient, una go eat di good of di land.
But if una refuse and rebel, una go dey devoured with sword, because di mouth of di Lord don talk am.”
How di faithful city don become prostitute! She full of justice before. Righteousness dey stay inside her, but now murderers.
Your silver don become dross, your wine mixed with water.
Your princes dey rebel and dey partner with thieves. Everyone love bribes and dey chase rewards. Dem no defend di fatherless, and di widow cause no dey come before dem.
Therefore di Lord, di Lord of Armies, di Mighty One of Israel, talk: “Ah, I go relieve myself of my adversaries and take revenge on my enemies.
I go turn my hand against you, and thoroughly purge away your dross, and remove all your alloy.
I go restore your judges as at di first, and your counselors as at di beginning. Afterward dem go call you di city of righteousness, di faithful city.”
Zion go dey redeemed with justice, and dem wey return go dey redeemed with righteousness.
But destruction of di rebels and sinners go dey together, and dem wey forsake di Lord go dey consumed.
Because dem go dey ashamed of di oaks wey una delight for, and una go dey confounded for di gardens wey una don choose.
Because una go be like oak wey im leaf dey fade, and like garden wey no get water.
Di strong man go be like tinder, and im work like spark. Dem both go burn together, and nobody go quench dem.
Di word wey Isaiah, Amoz pikin, see concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
E go happen for di latter days, say di mountain of di Lord house go dey established on di top of di mountains, and e go dey lifted up above di hills. All nations go flow to am.

Many peoples go go and talk say, “Come, make we go up to di mountain of di Lord, to di house of di God of Jacob, and e go teach us im ways, and we go waka for im paths.” Because from Zion di law go go out, and di word of di Lord from Jerusalem.

E go judge between di nations, and go settle matters for many peoples. Dem go beat dem swords into plowshares, and dem spears into pruning hooks. Nation no go lift up sword against nation, neither dem go learn war again.
Una house of Jacob, come, make we waka for di light of di Lord.

Because you don forsake your people, di house of Jacob, because dem full of customs from di east, and dem dey practice divination like di Philistines, and dem dey strike hands with foreigners pikin dem.
Dem land full of silver and gold, and dem treasures no get end. Dem land full of horses, and dem chariots no get end.
Dem land full of idols. Dem dey worship di work of dem own hands, wetin dem own fingers don make.
Man don dey brought low, and mankind don dey humbled, so no forgive dem.
Enter di rock, and hide for di dust, for fear of di Lord, and for di glory of im majesty.
Di lofty looks of man go dey brought low, and di pride of men go dey bowed down. Di Lord alone go dey exalted for dat day.
Because di day of di Lord of Armies go dey upon everyone wey proud and lofty, and upon everyone wey dem lift up, and e go dey brought low;
and upon all di cedars of Lebanon, wey high and lifted up, and upon all di oaks of Bashan;
and upon all di high mountains, and upon all di hills wey dem lift up;
and upon every high tower, and upon every fortified wall;
and upon all di ships of Tarshish, and upon all di beautiful sailing vessels.
Di pride of man go dey bowed down, and di loftiness of men go dey brought low. Di Lord alone go dey exalted for dat day.
Di idols go completely pass away.
Men go enter di caves of di rocks, and di holes of di earth, for fear of di Lord, and for di glory of im majesty, when e rise up to shake di earth mightily.
For dat day, men go throw away dem idols of silver, and dem idols of gold, wey dem make each one for imself to worship, to di moles and to di bats;
to go enter di caves of di rocks, and di clefts of di rugged rocks, for fear of di Lord, and for di glory of im majesty, when e rise up to shake di earth mightily.
Stop to trust man, wey im breath dey im nostrils, because wetin e be worth?
Because see, di Lord, di Lord of Armies, dey take away from Jerusalem and from Judah support and supply, di whole supply of bread and di whole supply of water;
di mighty man and di soldier, di judge and di prophet, di diviner and di elder;
di captain of 50, di honourable man, di counselor, di skilful craftsman and di expert enchanter.
I go make boys dey be dem princes, and babies go rule over dem.
Di people go dey oppressed, everyone by another, and everyone by im neighbour. Di youth go behave proudly against di elder, and di base against di honourable.
When man go take hold of im brother for im papa house, say, “You get cloak, you go be our ruler, and make dis ruin dey under your hand,”
for dat day e go cry out say, “I no go be healer. For my house no food dey and no cloak. No make me ruler of di people.”
Because Jerusalem don stumble, and Judah don fall, because dem tongue and dem doings dey against di Lord, to provoke di eyes of im glory.
Dem look dey witness against dem, and dem dey declare dem sin like Sodom. Dem no hide am. Woe to dem soul! Because dem don bring evil upon demselves.
Tell di righteous say e go dey well, because dem go eat di fruit of dem doings.
Woe to di wicked! E go dey bad for am, because wetin im hands don do go dey done to am.
As for my people, pikin dem na dem oppressors, and women dey rule over dem. My people, dem wey lead you dey lead you astray, and dem dey confuse di way of your paths.
Di Lord stand up to contend, and e stand to judge di peoples.
Di Lord go enter judgment with di elders of im people and im princes: “Na una don devour di vineyard. Di plunder of di poor dey inside una houses.
Wetin una mean say una dey crush my people and grind di face of di poor?” talk di Lord, di Lord of Armies.
Di Lord talk: “Because di daughters of Zion dey proud, and dey waka with outstretched necks and flirting eyes, dey waka mincingly as dem dey go, dey make jingling with dem feet,
so di Lord go strike with scab di crown of di head of di daughters of Zion, and di Lord go make dem forehead bare.”
For dat day di Lord go take away di beauty of dem anklets, headbands, crescent ornaments,
pendants, bracelets, veils,
headdresses, ankle chains, sashes, perfume boxes, charms,
signet rings, nose rings,
festal robes, mantles, cloaks, purses,
hand mirrors, fine linen garments, turbans and shawls.

E go happen say instead of sweet perfume, rottenness go dey; and instead of sash, rope; and instead of well-set hair, baldness; and instead of fine clothing, sackcloth; and branding instead of beauty.
Your men go fall by di sword, and your mighty men for war.
Her gates go lament and mourn, and she go dey desolate, sitting on di ground.
For dat day seven women go hold one man, say, “We go chop our own food, and wear our own clothes; only make we carry your name. Take away our shame.”
For dat day di branch of di Lord go dey beautiful and glorious, and di fruit of di land go dey excellent and lovely for dem wey escape of Israel.
E go happen say dem wey remain for Zion and dem wey dey left for Jerusalem go dey called holy, everyone wey dem write among di living for Jerusalem;
when di Lord don wash away di filth of di daughters of Zion, and don purge di blood of Jerusalem from inside am, by di spirit of judgment and by di spirit of burning.
Di Lord go create over di whole place of Mount Zion, and over her assemblies, cloud and smoke by day, and di shining of flaming fire by night; because over all di glory go be canopy.
Dere go dey shelter wey go give shade from heat for daytime, and refuge and shelter from storm and from rain.
Make I sing for my beloved di song of my beloved concerning im vineyard. My beloved get vineyard for very fruitful hill.
E dig am up, gather out di stones, plant am with di choicest vine, build tower inside am, and cut one winepress inside am. E expect say e go produce good grapes, but e produce wild grapes.
Now, una wey dey live for Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge, I beg una, between me and my vineyard.
Wetin more fit don dey do for my vineyard, wey I never do for am? Why, when I expect say e go produce good grapes, e produce wild grapes?
Now go to, I go tell una wetin I go do to my vineyard. I go take away im hedge, and e go dey eaten up. I go break down im wall, and e go dey trampled down.
I go lay am waste. E no go dey pruned or hoed, but briers and thorns go grow up. I go also command di clouds say make dem no rain on am.
Because di vineyard of di Lord of Armies na di house of Israel, and di men of Judah na im pleasant plant. E look for justice, but see, oppression; for righteousness, but see, cry of distress.
Woe to dem wey join house to house, wey lay field to field, until no room dey, and una dey dwell alone for di middle of di land!
Di Lord of Armies don swear for my ears: “Surely many houses go dey desolate, even great and fair ones, without inhabitant.
Because 10 acres of vineyard go yield one bath, and one homer of seed go yield one ephah.”
Woe to dem wey rise up early for morning, so that dem go follow strong drink, wey continue until night, till wine inflame dem!
Di harp and di lyre, di tambourine and di flute, and wine dey for dem feasts, but dem no regard di work of di Lord, neither dem consider di operation of im hands.
Therefore my people don go into captivity for lack of knowledge. Dem honourable men dey hungry, and dem multitude dry with thirst.
Therefore Sheol don enlarge her desire, and open her mouth without measure. Dem glory, dem multitude, dem pomp, and di one wey dey rejoice among dem go go down into am.
Man don dey brought low, and mankind don dey humbled, and di eyes of di lofty dey humbled;
but di Lord of Armies dey exalted for justice, and God wey dey holy dey show imself holy for righteousness.
Den di lambs go graze as for dem pasture, and strangers go eat di waste places of di rich.
Woe to dem wey draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, and wey sin dey like cart rope;
wey talk say, “Make e hurry, make e speed im work, so that we fit see am; and make di counsel of di Holy One of Israel draw near and come, so that we go know am!”
Woe to dem wey call evil good, and good evil; wey put darkness for light, and light for darkness; wey put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!
Woe to dem wey wise for dem own eyes, and clever for dem own sight!
Woe to dem wey dey mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mix strong drink;
wey justify di wicked for reward, and take away di righteousness of di righteous man from am!

Therefore as di tongue of fire devour di stubble, and as dry grass sink down for di flame, so dem root go be like rottenness, and dem blossom go go up like dust, because dem don reject di law of di Lord of Armies, and despise di word of di Holy One of Israel.

Therefore di anger of di Lord dey burn against im people, and e don stretch out im hand against dem and strike dem. Di mountains dey tremble, and dem dead bodies dey like refuse for di middle of di streets. For all dis, im anger no turn away, but im hand still dey stretched out.
E go lift up banner to di nations from far, and go whistle to dem from di end of di earth. See, dem go come with speed, swiftly.
None go dey weary or stumble among dem. None go slumber or sleep. Neither di belt of dem waist go dey loosed, nor di strap of dem sandals broken;
whose arrows sharp, and all dem bows bent. Dem horses hoofs go dey counted like flint, and dem wheels like whirlwind.
Dem roaring go be like lioness. Dem go roar like young lions. Yes, dem go roar and seize di prey, and carry am off safe, and none go deliver am.
For dat day dem go roar against dem like di roaring of di sea. If one look to di land, see, darkness and distress. Di light dey darkened for di clouds of am.
For di year wey King Uzziah die, I see di Lord sitting on throne, high and lifted up, and im train fill di temple.
Above am stand seraphim. Each one get six wings. With two e cover im face, with two e cover im feet, and with two e dey fly.
One cry to another, and talk say, “Holy, holy, holy, na di Lord of Armies! Im glory full all di earth!”
Di foundations of di thresholds shake at di voice of im wey cry out, and di house full of smoke.
Den I talk say, “Woe to me! Because I don dey ruined, because I be man wey im lips dirty, and I dey live among people wey dem lips dirty, because my eyes don see di King, di Lord of Armies!”
Den one of di seraphim fly to me, wey get live coal for im hand, wey e don take with tongs from di altar.
E touch my mouth with am, and talk say, “See, dis don touch your lips. Your iniquity don dey taken away, and your sin don dey forgiven.”
I hear di voice of di Lord, wey talk say, “Who I go send, and who go go for us?” Den I talk say, “Here I dey. Send me!”
E talk say, “Go, and tell dis people, ‘Hear indeed, but no understand. See indeed, but no perceive.’
Make di heart of dis people fat, make dem ears heavy, and shut dem eyes, so that dem no go see with dem eyes, hear with dem ears, understand with dem heart, and turn again and dey healed.”
Den I talk say, “Lord, how long?” E answer, “Until cities dey wasted without inhabitant, houses without man, and di land dey utterly desolate,
and di Lord don remove men far away, and di forsaken places plenty for di middle of di land.
If still one tenth remain inside am, e go dey burned again, like terebinth or like oak, wey im stump remain when dem cut dem down. So di holy seed na di stump inside am.”

For di days of Ahaz, Jotham pikin, Uzziah pikin, king of Judah, Rezin di king of Syria and Pekah, Remaliah pikin, king of Israel, go up to Jerusalem to war against am, but dem no fit prevail against am.
Dem tell di house of David say, “Syria don join with Ephraim.” Im heart shake, and di heart of im people, as di trees of di forest dey shake with di wind.
Den di Lord talk to Isaiah, “Go out now to meet Ahaz, you and Shear Jashub your pikin, for di end of di conduit of di upper pool, for di highway of di fuller field.
Tell am, ‘Take care, and dey quiet. No fear, neither make your heart faint, because of dis two tails of smoking firebrands, because of di fierce anger of Rezin and Syria and di son of Remaliah.
Because Syria, Ephraim and Remaliah pikin don plan evil against you, say,
“Make we go up against Judah, and vex am, and make we break into am for us, and set king inside am, even di son of Tabeel.”
Di Lord God talk, “E no go stand, neither e go happen.
Because di head of Syria na Damascus, and di head of Damascus na Rezin. Within 65 years Ephraim go dey broken, so that e no go be people again.
Di head of Ephraim na Samaria, and di head of Samaria na Remaliah pikin. If una no believe, surely una no go dey established.”’”
Di Lord talk again to Ahaz, say,
“Ask one sign from di Lord your God. Ask am for di depth, or for di height above.”
But Ahaz talk say, “I no go ask, neither I go test di Lord.”
E talk say, “Hear now, house of David. Na small thing say una tire men, say una go tire my God too?
Therefore di Lord imself go give una sign. See, di virgin go conceive and bear son, and go call im name Immanuel.
E go eat butter and honey when e know to refuse di evil and choose di good.
Because before di child go know to refuse di evil and choose di good, di land wey you dey fear for im two kings go dey forsaken.
Di Lord go bring upon you, upon your people and upon your papa house, days wey no come since di day wey Ephraim depart from Judah, even di king of Assyria.”
For dat day, di Lord go whistle for di fly wey dey di farthest part of di rivers of Egypt, and for di bee wey dey di land of Assyria.
Dem go come, and dem all go rest for di desolate valleys, for di clefts of di rocks, for all di thorn bushes and for all di watering places.
For dat day di Lord go shave with razor wey dem hire beyond di River, even with di king of Assyria, di head and di hair of di feet, and e go also consume di beard.
For dat day, man go keep alive one young cow and two sheep;
and e go happen say because of di abundance of milk wey dem go give, e go eat butter, because everyone wey remain for di land go eat butter and honey.
For dat day, every place where 1,000 vines dey, worth 1,000 pieces of silver, go be for briers and thorns.
Men go go dere with arrows and with bow, because all di land go be briers and thorns.
As for all di hills wey dem dey dig with hoe, no one go go dere for fear of briers and thorns, but e go be place for sending out oxen and for di treading of sheep.
Di Lord talk to me, “Take big tablet, and write for am with man pen: ‘Maher Shalal Hash Baz.’
I go take faithful witnesses to record for me, Uriah di priest and Zechariah, Jeberekiah pikin.”
I go to di prophetess, and she conceive and born son. Den di Lord talk to me, “Call im name Maher Shalal Hash Baz.
Because before di child go know how to cry ‘My papa’ and ‘My mama,’ di riches of Damascus and di plunder of Samaria go dey carried away before di king of Assyria.”
Di Lord talk to me again,
“Because dis people don refuse di waters of Shiloah wey dey flow softly, and dey rejoice with Rezin and Remaliah pikin,
now therefore, see, di Lord dey bring up upon dem di waters of di River, strong and many, even di king of Assyria and all im glory. E go come up over all im channels, and go over all im banks.
E go sweep through Judah. E go overflow and pass over. E go reach even to di neck, and di stretching out of im wings go fill di breadth of your land, Immanuel.”
Make una dey broken, una peoples, and una go dey shattered! Listen, all una far countries! Gird una yourselves, and una go dey shattered! Gird una yourselves, and una go dey shattered!
Take counsel together, and e go come to nothing. Speak di word, and e no go stand, because God dey with us.
Because di Lord talk dis to me with strong hand, and instruct me no to waka for di way of dis people, say,
“No call conspiracy all wey dis people call conspiracy. No fear wetin dem fear, neither dey afraid.
Di Lord of Armies, na am una must regard as holy. Make am be your fear, and make am be your dread.
E go be sanctuary, but e go also be stone of stumbling and rock of offence to di two houses of Israel, trap and snare to di people wey dey live for Jerusalem.
Many go stumble over am. Dem go fall, dey broken, dey snared and dey taken.”
Bind up di testimony, seal di law among my disciples.
I go wait for di Lord, wey dey hide im face from di house of Jacob, and I go hope for am.
See, I and di children wey di Lord don give me dey for signs and for wonders for Israel from di Lord of Armies, wey dey live for Mount Zion.
When dem talk to una say, “Seek di mediums and di wizards wey chirp and mutter,” no be say people suppose seek dem God? Dem suppose seek di dead for di living?
To di law and to di testimony! If dem no speak according to dis word, e dey surely because no light dey inside dem.
Dem go pass through am, hard pressed and hungry. E go happen say when dem dey hungry, dem go dey furious, and curse dem king and dem God, and look upward.
Dem go look to di earth, and see trouble, darkness and gloom of anguish. Dem go dey driven into thick darkness.

But dere go dey no more gloom for her wey dey for distress. For di former time e bring di land of Zebulun and di land of Naphtali into contempt, but for di latter time e don make am glorious, by di way of di sea, beyond di Jordan, Galilee of di nations.
Di people wey waka for darkness don see great light. Dem wey dey live for di land of di shadow of death, light don shine on dem.
You don multiply di nation. You don increase im joy. Dem dey rejoice before you like joy for harvest, as men dey rejoice when dem dey divide plunder.
Because di yoke of im burden, and di rod for im shoulder, di rod of im oppressor, you don break am as for di day of Midian.
Because every boot of di armed man for di noisy battle, and di garment wey dem roll for blood, go be for burning, fuel of fire.
Because pikin don born for us, son don dey given to us; and di government go dey upon im shoulder. Dem go call im name Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Papa, Prince of Peace.

Of di increase of im government and of peace, no end go dey, upon di throne of David and upon im kingdom, to establish am and to uphold am with justice and with righteousness from dat time forward and forever. Di zeal of di Lord of Armies go perform dis.
Di Lord send word into Jacob, and e don fall upon Israel.
All di people go know, even Ephraim and di inhabitant of Samaria, wey dey talk with pride and arrogance of heart:
“Di bricks don fall, but we go rebuild with dressed stones. Di sycamore trees dem don cut down, but we go change dem for cedars.”
Therefore di Lord go set up di adversaries of Rezin against am, and go stir up im enemies,
di Syrians for front and di Philistines for back, and dem go devour Israel with open mouth. For all dis, im anger no turn away, but im hand still dey stretched out.
Yet di people no turn to am wey strike dem, neither dem seek di Lord of Armies.
So di Lord go cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, for one day.
Di elder and honourable man na di head, and di prophet wey teach lies na di tail.
Because dem wey lead dis people dey cause dem to err, and dem wey dey led by dem dey swallowed up.

Therefore di Lord no go rejoice over dem young men, neither go have compassion on dem fatherless and widows, because everyone na godless and evildoer, and every mouth dey speak folly. For all dis, im anger no turn away, but im hand still dey stretched out.
Because wickedness dey burn like fire. E dey devour briers and thorns. Yes, e dey kindle for di thickets of di forest, and dem dey roll upward for column of smoke.
Through di wrath of di Lord of Armies di land dey burnt up, and di people dey like fuel of fire. No man dey spare im brother.
Dem dey snatch for di right hand, and dey hungry, and dem dey eat for di left hand, and dem no dey satisfied. Everyone dey eat di flesh of im own arm:
Manasseh dey devour Ephraim, and Ephraim dey devour Manasseh, and dem together dey against Judah. For all dis, im anger no turn away, but im hand still dey stretched out.
Woe to dem wey decree unrighteous decrees, and to di writers wey write oppression;
to turn away di needy from justice, and to rob di poor of my people of dem right, so that widows fit dey dem prey, and that dem go plunder di fatherless!
Wetin una go do for di day of visitation, and for di destruction wey go come from far? To who una go flee for help? Where una go leave una glory?
Dem go only bow down under di prisoners, and dem go fall under di slain. For all dis, im anger no turn away, but im hand still dey stretched out.
Woe to Assyria, di rod of my anger, di staff wey dey dem hand na my indignation!
I go send am against godless nation, and against di people of my wrath I go give am charge, to take di plunder, to seize di prey, and to tread dem down like di mire of di streets.
But e no mean so, neither im heart think so; but na for im heart to destroy, and to cut off nations no few.
Because e talk say, “No be my princes all kings?
No be Calno like Carchemish? No be Hamath like Arpad? No be Samaria like Damascus?
As my hand don find di kingdoms of di idols, wey dem graven images pass dem for Jerusalem and for Samaria,
as I don do to Samaria and to her idols, no go I do so to Jerusalem and to her idols?”
E go happen say when di Lord don perform all im work for Mount Zion and for Jerusalem, I go punish di fruit of di arrogant heart of di king of Assyria, and di glory of im haughty looks.

Because e talk say, “By di strength of my hand I don do am, and by my wisdom, because I get understanding. I don remove di boundaries of di peoples, and I don rob dem treasures, and like mighty man I don bring down dem wey sit on thrones.
My hand don find like nest di riches of di peoples, and as one gather eggs wey dem leave, I don gather all di earth. Nobody move wing, or open mouth, or chirp.”
Di axe fit boast against di one wey dey chop with am? Di saw fit magnify imself against di one wey dey use am? As if rod go shake dem wey lift am up, or as if staff go lift up wetin no be wood!
Therefore di Lord, di Lord of Armies, go send among im fat ones leanness, and under im glory e go kindle burning like burning of fire.
Di light of Israel go become fire, and im Holy One flame, and e go burn and devour im thorns and im briers for one day.
E go consume di glory of im forest and of im fruitful field, both soul and body, and e go be like when sick man waste away.
Di rest of di trees of im forest go dey few, so that child fit write dem down.
E go happen for dat day, say di remnant of Israel, and dem wey don escape of di house of Jacob, no go again lean on di one wey strike dem, but go lean on di Lord, di Holy One of Israel, for truth.
Di remnant go return, di remnant of Jacob, to di mighty God.
Because though your people, Israel, be like di sand of di sea, only remnant of dem go return. Destruction don dey decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
Because di Lord, di Lord of Armies, go complete di destruction wey dem decree for di middle of all di land.
Therefore di Lord, di Lord of Armies, talk: “My people wey dey live for Zion, no fear Assyria wey dey strike una with rod, and lift up im staff against una as Egypt do.
Because yet small while, and di indignation go finish, and my anger go dey for dem destruction.”
Di Lord of Armies go stir up scourge for am, as di striking of Midian for di rock of Oreb. As im rod dey over di sea, so e go lift am up as e do for Egypt.
For dat day, im burden go dey taken away from your shoulder, and im yoke from your neck, and di yoke go dey destroyed because of fatness.
E don come to Aiath. E don pass through Migron. For Michmash e store im baggage.
Dem don cross di pass. Dem don lodge for Geba. Ramah tremble. Gibeah of Saul don flee.
Cry aloud with your voice, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah don flee. Di inhabitants of Gebim don gather demselves to flee.
Dis very day e go halt for Nob. E dey shake im fist at di mountain of di daughter of Zion, di hill of Jerusalem.
See, di Lord, di Lord of Armies, go lop di boughs with terror. Di tall ones go dey cut down, and di lofty go dey brought low.
E go cut down di thickets of di forest with iron, and Lebanon go fall by mighty one.
